senses.gloss:
Khanitra, a ‘shovel’ or ‘spade’ for digging, is mentioned in the Rigveda and later.
Foot notes i. 179, 6 (possibly metaphorical: see Oldenberg. ṛgveda-Noten, 1, 172; the passage is obscure).
Lāṭyāyana śrauta sūtra, viii. 2, 4, etc.

Khanitrima, ‘produced by digging,’ as an epithet of āpaḥ, ‘waters,’ clearly refers to artificial water channels used for irrigation, as practised in the times of the Rigveda and the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes vii. 49, 2.
i. 6, 4; xix. 2, 2.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 236; Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 5, 466.
